note: The two sets are identical except for the framing of the ∂P/∂θ dependence claim: Set A states the dependence as the value, while Set B calls it an aerodynamic property and moves the dependence into conditions. Both capture the same facts from the same quote, so neither is more faithful overall. Both also repeat the ωφn = 0.6 rad/s and ζφ = 0.6–0.7 targets twice (once bound to the blade-pitch controller, once to the rotor-speed error response) and both omit the qualitative roles of the derivative, proportional and integral terms and the need to compensate the generator-torque negative damping.
remarks: Both sets duplicate the Ref. [10] design targets (0.6 rad/s and 0.6–0.7) under two entity names; these should be merged. Both miss the page's statements that the derivative term increases effective drivetrain inertia, the proportional term adds damping, the integral term adds restoring, and that the negative damping from the generator-torque controller must be compensated by the proportional term. The text layer is heavily garbled around Eqs. (7-11)–(7-15), but the rendered equations in the image are legible and match the extracted formulas.
